subject.title: All LLM API calls time out simultaneously despite APIs being reachable (multi-agent concurrency issue)

question: Should this issue remain the canonical current-main live-repro target for the four-agent Telegram/provider timeout pattern, or should maintainers split the remaining work into narrower provider, Telegram, session-lock, and launch-default issues now?
rationale: The report crosses fallback policy, provider transport, Telegram runner concurrency, session locking, and launch/runtime defaults; source inspection shows partial mitigations but not enough proof to choose a single safe implementation boundary automatically.

options.title: Require canonical live repro
options.body: Keep this issue open and require a current-main four-agent Telegram trace before choosing a code or config change.

options.title: Split into narrower issues
options.body: Create explicit owner-scoped follow-ups for provider timeout budgeting, Telegram concurrency, session locks, and launch defaults if maintainers decide this report is too broad.

options.title: Close after mitigation proof
options.body: Close only if a current-main live run comparable to the original setup shows the all-provider timeout pattern no longer occurs.

recommendation.title: Require canonical live repro
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open and require a current-main four-agent Telegram trace before choosing a code or config change.

likelyOwner.reason: altaywtf supplied live proof and merged the closest fallback mitigation, making them the best available owner for deciding whether the remaining evidence is sufficient or needs a narrower owner split.
